messages:
Alex K: Quick sync — sales pushed for a pricing doc we can hand to large prospects. They want clear tiers + optional add-ons (burst, SLA, private deploy pack). Need product + legal tradeoffs before EOD.
Maria G: thanks — can we scope what 'burst' actually means? two asks come up: 1) short spikes for hosted customers, 2) overage/burst for Dedicated with reserved pools.
Jamal R: Sales context: enterprise prospects will pay for reservable throughput but want guaranteed burst for big events (marketing launches). They don't want extra negotiation every time. Prefer a predictable add-on price.
Sara L: Legal note: any committed capacity + burst guarantees will require explicit terms in contract (billing triggers, caps, etc.). Also watch out for refund language if we throttle.
Lee N: Eng constraints: Dedicated pools can provision burst via pre-warmed nodes or elastic shared pool. Pre-warming costs us; shared pool can degrade latency. Need SLO/backstop policy.
Maria G: Proposed draft tiering (informal):
- Starter: hosted, soft quotas, no SLA, basic metrics
- Scale: hosted + Dedicated lite option, 99.9% best-effort, optional burst add-on
- Enterprise: Dedicated, 99.95% SLA, burst credits, private deploy add-on
We need numbers for quotas and pricing.
Jamal R: Customers expect burst to be expressed as 'X minutes at Y QPS' or 'N tokens of burst credits per month'. Prefer credits model.
Alex K: Good. Let's align on launch criteria before we price. My suggested GA checklist:
```
- 3 pilot customers across different verticals (SaaS, platform, marketplace)
- SLAs validated on Dedicated (latency + availability) under burst scenarios
- Billing: invoice + stripe metered flows for burst credits
- Legal: contract language for burst caps, chargebacks, refund policy
- Console: UI to buy/apply burst credits and visibility for customers
```
Maria G: + add monitoring/alerting: cost-per-token dashboard and anomaly detection. If burst causes runaway cost, we need auto-throttle.
Lee N: Implementation note: include an automatic fallback that routes to a lower-cost model variant when burst pool is exhausted. That reduces cost exposure.
Sara L: For contract constraints, we'll need: max burst per billing period, pre-approval flow for multi-month bursts, and a clause about emergency throttling with notice. I'll draft language.
Jamal R: Pricing ask from field: price burst credits at ~2x normal committed unit cost to deter abuse but still be affordable. Also offer a one-time buy for emergency credit.
Alex K: That pricing multiplier seems reasonable as starting guidance. Also consider volume discounts for annual commitments.
Maria G: UX question: should burst be auto-topup? i.e., customer hits threshold -> auto-buys small pack? Pros: fewer interruptions. Cons: complexity & potential billing surprise.
Jamal R: Customers want control; default off, opt-in with clear consent. Auto-topup only for ops-approved accounts.
Lee N: From infra side, implement flags: `burst_auto_topup: true|false`, `burst_cap_monthly`, `burst_fallback_policy`. We'll provide API and console surfaces.
ProductBot: Reminder: roadmap slot for "Burst Add-on" is in Q2 planning epic #PRD-842. Link: https://redwood.example/epics/PRD-842
Alex K: OK action items:
- Sara to draft contract clauses (due tomorrow)
- Lee to estimate infra cost delta & risk (2-day spike estimate)
- Maria to draft pricing bands + launch GA checklist language by EOD
- Jamal to collect top 5 prospect asks and sample deal terms
We'll reconvene Friday 10:30 PT to finalize. @all please add blockers to the PRD. :thumbsup:
Maria G: noted and will include a small changelog for product docs.
Sara L: I'll post a redline draft to the thread when ready.
Lee N: I'll upload a quick cost-model spreadsheet (ETA 48hrs).
Jamal R: I'll add sample contract redlines teams are requesting.
Alex K: Great. Final note: avoid permanent per-customer exceptions in the pricing matrix; prefer documented add-ons to keep ops scalable.
ProductBot: Meeting scheduled: Friday 10:30 PT in #product (invite sent).
